new_sources.title: ResearchClawBench: A Benchmark for End-to-End Autonomous Scientific Research
Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
scBench-Long: Verifiable Benchmarking of Long-Horizon Single-Cell Biology

candidate_mechanisms.description: For a scientifically consequential subproblem with a machine-checkable target, construct executable tasks whose reference answer is generated by canonical code, cross-validated against the published claim, and expert-audited. Train/optimize the agent on synthetic executable tasks using outcome-grounded rewards for the actual inferential quantity rather than rewarding fluent reports or code execution alone.
quantitative_evidence: P-Bench contains 425 open-ended hypothesis-testing tasks spanning economics, biology, and medicine; every reference p-value/decision is tied to a logged canonical execution and expert audit.
Fisher-R1-14B P-Hard Strict pass@1 reaches 33.0% versus DeepSeek-V4-Pro 26.3%, GPT-5.4 30.5%, and its Qwen2.5-Coder-14B backbone 23.7%; P-Easy Strict pass@1 reaches 64.2% versus backbone 41.4%.

On the 7B ablation, P-Hard Strict pass@1 is 13.2% for the backbone, 25.2% with DAPO alone, 14.3% with SFT alone, and 30.6% with SFT+DAPO. P-Easy Strict pass@1 is 36.3%, 44.4%, 30.2%, and 65.7%, respectively.
The paper reports Fisher-R1-14B has 21% average relative single-trial improvement over DeepSeek-V4-Pro, with gains up to 26% on the hardest tasks.
candidate_mechanisms.causal_evidence: The 7B ablation supports an interaction: verified-outcome RL directly improves single-run correctness, while SFT alone mainly broadens pass@3; SFT warm-start plus RL is best on every reported metric. The paper's synthetic training corpus is separate from P-Bench and embedding checks found no near-duplicate evaluation prompts.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Single hypothesis tests with canonical/reference analyses; the reward does not explicitly score method identity because multiple methods can be defensible. It does not yet cover multiple-testing correction or full experimental discovery. Canonical analyses can themselves be imperfect, so expert auditing and source provenance remain necessary.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O's evaluator architecture: wherever a research subproblem admits an executable, audited domain oracle, use that grounded signal for learning/evaluation rather than a generic LLM judge. Also separate inferential correctness from mere code success.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Use a deterministic, reproducible endpoint criterion as the actual scientific success signal while retaining model-based trajectory rubrics only as dense diagnostics for partial progress and chokepoint localization. Evaluate multiple independent replicates because one successful trajectory is not evidence of reliable long-horizon competence.
quantitative_evidence: Across 1,068 completed trajectories and 21 long-horizon single-cell evaluations, the strongest model-harness pair passed 16/63 runs (25.4%, Wilson 95% CI 16.3–37.3), passed at least one replicate on 8/21 evaluations, but all three replicates on only 2/21.
Overall deterministic endpoint success was 125/1,068 trajectories (11.7%).

Four rubric judges were mutually consistent for diagnostics (mean pairwise correlation 0.90), yet rubric score correlated only weakly with deterministic endpoint success: Pearson r=0.29, Spearman rho=0.30, AUC=0.77. The highest rubric decile contained only 47/106 endpoint successes.
The same model's performance changed materially with harness: GPT-5.4 passed 6/63 under PI but 2/63 under OpenAI Codex; Claude Opus 4.8 passed 16/63 with Claude Code versus 13/63 with PI.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Single-cell biology and the benchmark's controlled-answer endpoint. Harness comparisons are not fully controlled architecture ablations because prompts/tools/runtime details can differ. Rubric calibration is benchmark-specific.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O evaluation: keep deterministic/external endpoint evidence separate from model-judge diagnostics, record replicate robustness instead of best-run success, and treat execution harness/context as part of the tested configuration rather than a neutral wrapper.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Evaluate full scientific rediscovery from a question, related literature, and raw data while hiding the target paper from the agent. Expert-curated weighted rubrics are anchored to concrete target-paper scientific artifacts, with a reference-level threshold rather than exposing the answer during search.
quantitative_evidence: 40 tasks across 10 scientific domains. The strongest autonomous system, Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.6, averages 21.5/100; the best autonomous result selected per task averages 24.6. A score of 50 is defined as target-paper-level evidence.
Among native LLMs under a lightweight ResearchHarness, Claude Opus 4.7 averages 20.7; the per-task LLM frontier mean is 26.5.
Failures concentrate in experimental-protocol mismatch, evidence mismatch, and missing scientific core.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: The reference-anchored score is still rubric/judge mediated and 50 is a benchmark operational threshold, not proof of real novel discovery. Cross-system comparisons include different base models and agent scaffolds.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High as an evaluation candidate for O because it reduces target-answer leakage and measures full evidence production rather than local stage competence. It also provides a concrete held-out external baseline showing current end-to-end scientist systems remain far below reference-level rediscovery.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Frontier agents can identify outliers/assumption problems, execute valid code, and still choose an inappropriate inferential method that yields a false discovery. P-Bench specifically shows a large gap between conclusion-only correctness and strict p-value-grounded correctness.
new_failure_evidence.scope: P-Bench single-test tasks and evaluated models.
new_failure_evidence.implication: For empirical research, result interpretation must be checked against domain assumptions and the executed statistic; runnable analysis is not enough.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Rubric judges agree strongly with each other but correlate only modestly with deterministic endpoint success. High judge agreement therefore does not imply high validity against the scientific endpoint.
new_failure_evidence.scope: scBench-Long's four judges and deterministic controlled-answer tasks.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Evaluator agreement/quorum should not be treated as sufficient validity evidence; calibration against external/deterministic outcomes is necessary.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Agents frequently execute plausible analyses but fail to integrate modalities, preserve the correct comparison/protocol, distinguish association from mechanism, or recover the central scientific claim. ResearchClawBench likewise finds protocol/evidence/core mismatches as dominant failures.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Single-cell long-horizon tasks and ResearchClawBench's 40 multi-domain tasks; failure taxonomies differ and should not be numerically pooled.
new_failure_evidence.implication: O should evaluate whether experiments answer the intended causal/scientific question, not just whether each local stage is coherent or executable.

new_failure_evidence.observation: The strongest pair obtained at least one successful replicate on 8/21 tasks but succeeded on all three replicates for only 2/21, showing a large gap between any-pass capability and reliable repeated success.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Three replicates per evaluated model-harness/task in scBench-Long.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Report both capability and robustness; do not promote a mechanism based only on one lucky successful run.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not use Fisher-R1's canonical p-value as a universal model for scientific truth. It is powerful because this subproblem admits audited executable reference analyses; many open research questions do not.
Do not replace deterministic endpoints with highly agreeing LLM rubrics; scBench-Long directly shows agreement and validity are distinct.
Do not infer a general ranking of Claude Code, PI, Codex, or ResearchHarness from these benchmark rows; base models, tools, and tasks differ. Treat harness as part of the configuration.
ResearchClawBench RADS scores above 50 indicate reference-surpassing evidence potential, not automatically validated discoveries.
next_queries: Search primary 2026 work on causal/statistical/reproducibility validators embedded inside full autonomous research loops, beyond isolated P-Bench hypothesis testing.
Inspect ResearchClawBench detailed error taxonomy and whether any controlled scaffold/harness interventions reduce protocol mismatch or evidence mismatch.
Search benchmarks with hidden target papers/raw data that include deterministic or execution-grounded endpoints rather than predominantly rubric judges.
Find scientist-agent studies reporting repeated-run robustness and variance as primary metrics, especially where a mechanism improves all-replicate success rather than best-of-N.
Find external evidence that combines evidence graphs/provenance-before-prose with executable statistical/formal oracles in one end-to-end system.
